newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by domestic buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by domestic buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up in heavy trade on Wednesday led by local buying across the board, brokers said.

Foreign buying was low as overseas buyers waited to see if the market could be sustained at current levels, but their absence was not due to recent gains on Wall Street keeping global funds away, they said.
The all share index closed 12.18 points up at 739.50. Price gains led declines by 41 to eight. Aitken Spence rose 1.25 rupees to 155.25, and Commercial Bank 10 to 210.
"The market was supported entirely by local investors, as foreigners waited to see if the current upward movement could be sustained," said Rohan Fernando of CT Smith Stock Brokers.
Turnover was 115.9 million rupees, led by Colombo Dockyard, John Keells Holdings, Grain Elevators and Lion Brewery.
"Many local institutional investors were switching to equities from treasury bills and bonds, where rates have fallen steadily this year," said a broker who declined to be identified.
Yields of treasury bonds and bills have fallen due to improved money supply after the Central Bank cut reserve ratios of commercial banks by three percent.
Parcels of 3.8 million shares of Kegalle Plantations and 1.55 million of Kelani Valley came on bid on an all-or-none basis, at 31.50 rupees and 31 rupees, respectively.
